from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial Setup
        title = "The Prerequisite: The Bernoulli Trial"
        lines = [
            "Every complex probability starts with a single simple trial.",
            "Meet Byte. He either makes the shot or misses.",
            "We call this a Bernoulli Trial: Success or Failure."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Bernoulli Toggle Switch
        switch_label = Text("Bernoulli Trial", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(switch_label, "A3", scale_factor=0.8)
        switch_label.shift(RIGHT * 0.5)

        switch_rect = RoundedRectangle(height=0.8, width=1.6, corner_radius=0.4, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(switch_rect, "B3", "B4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        knob = Circle(radius=0.3, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=1)
        # Position knob inside the switch rect
        knob.move_to(switch_rect.get_left() + RIGHT * 0.4)
        
        success_label = Text("Success", color="#00FF00", font_size=20)
        failure_label = Text("Failure", color="#FF0000", font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(failure_label, "B2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(success_label, "B5", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(FadeIn(switch_label), FadeIn(switch_rect), FadeIn(knob), FadeIn(success_label), FadeIn(failure_label))
        
        # Flipping animation
        self.play(
            knob.animate.move_to(switch_rect.get_right() - RIGHT * 0.4),
            switch_rect.animate.set_fill("#00FF00", opacity=0.3),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.play(
            knob.animate.move_to(switch_rect.get_left() + RIGHT * 0.4),
            switch_rect.animate.set_fill("#FF0000", opacity=0.3),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Byte the Robot
        byte_body = Square(side_length=0.8, color="#58C4DD", fill_opacity=1)
        byte_head = Square(side_length=0.4, color="#58C4DD", fill_opacity=1).next_to(byte_body, UP, buff=0.1)
        eye_l = Dot(color=BLACK, radius=0.04).move_to(byte_head.get_center() + LEFT*0.1 + UP*0.05)
        eye_r = Dot(color=BLACK, radius=0.04).move_to(byte_head.get_center() + RIGHT*0.1 + UP*0.05)
        byte = VGroup(byte_body, byte_head, eye_l, eye_r)
        self.place_at_grid(byte, "E1", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Basketball Hoop
        hoop_pole = Line(self.grid["F5"], self.grid["D5"], color=WHITE)
        hoop_backboard = Rectangle(height=0.6, width=0.1, color=WHITE).next_to(hoop_pole.get_top(), LEFT, buff=0)
        hoop_rim = Ellipse(width=0.5, height=0.15, color="#FFFFFF").next_to(hoop_backboard, LEFT, buff=0).shift(DOWN*0.1)
        hoop = VGroup(hoop_pole, hoop_backboard, hoop_rim)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(byte), FadeIn(hoop))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Shooting the ball
        ball = Circle(radius=0.15, color="#FFA500", fill_opacity=1)
        ball.move_to(byte.get_top() + RIGHT*0.2)
        
        # Paths
        start_point = ball.get_center()
        success_end = hoop_rim.get_center()
        failure_end = hoop_rim.get_center() + DOWN*1.5 + RIGHT*0.5
        
        path_p = CurvedArrow(start_point, success_end, angle=-TAU/4, color="#00FF00")
        path_q = CurvedArrow(start_point, failure_end, angle=-TAU/6, color="#FF0000")
        
        # Using Text with slant=ITALIC instead of MathTex to avoid LaTeX dependency issues
        label_p = Text("p", slant=ITALIC, color="#00FF00", font_size=30).next_to(path_p, UP, buff=0.1)
        label_q = Text("1-p", slant=ITALIC, color="#FF0000", font_size=30).next_to(path_q, DOWN, buff=0.1)

        # Animate the paths and labels
        self.play(Create(path_p), FadeIn(label_p))
        self.play(Create(path_q), FadeIn(label_q))
        
        # Shot animation (Success)
        self.play(FadeIn(ball))
        self.play(MoveAlongPath(ball, path_p), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(ball.animate.shift(DOWN * 0.5), rate_func=there_and_back)
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(FadeOut(ball))
        
        # Reset ball for second trial visual
        ball.move_to(start_point)
        self.play(FadeIn(ball))
        self.play(MoveAlongPath(ball, path_q), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # End of section
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):

        self.setup_layout(
            "Defining the Binomial Distribution (The BINS Test)",

                'For a Binomial Distribution, we use the BINS test.', 
                'Outcomes must be Binary: a simple success or failure.', 
                'Each trial must be Independent from the previous ones.', 
                'We need a fixed Number of trials, like ten.', 
                'The probability of success must remain the Same throughout.'

        COLOR_B = "#58C4DD"
        COLOR_I = "#83C167"
        COLOR_N = "#FFFF00"

        b_letter = Text("B", font_size=60, color=COLOR_B)
        i_letter = Text("I", font_size=60, color=COLOR_I)
        n_letter = Text("N", font_size=60, color=COLOR_N)
        s_letter = Text("S", font_size=60, color=COLOR_S)

        self.place_at_grid(b_letter, "A3")
        self.place_at_grid(i_letter, "B3")
        self.place_at_grid(n_letter, "C3")
        self.place_at_grid(s_letter, "D3")

        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.play(
            FadeIn(b_letter),
            FadeIn(i_letter),
            FadeIn(n_letter),
            FadeIn(s_letter),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight 'B' (Binary), add checkmark and '2 outcomes'

        self.place_at_grid(check_b, "A2")

        self.play(
            b_letter.animate.scale(1.2),
            Write(check_b),

        self.play(b_letter.animate.scale(1/1.2), run_time=0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight 'I' (Independent), add checkmark and 'No influence'

        check_i = Text("✓", color=COLOR_I, font_size=40)
        self.place_at_grid(check_i, "B2")

        self.place_at_grid(desc_n, "C4")

        self.play(

            Write(check_n),
            FadeIn(desc_n),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.play(n_letter.animate.scale(1/1.2), run_time=0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===

        self.play(

            FadeIn(desc_s),
            run_time=1

        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Layout and Title
        title = Text("Section 4: The Binomial Distribution Formula", font_size=36)
        title.to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        self.add(title)
        
        # 2. Formula Display 
        # Using Text to avoid LaTeX dependency (MathTex requires 'latex' installed)
        formula = Text(
            "P(X = k) = nCk * p^k * (1-p)^(n-k)",
            font_size=32,
            color=YELLOW
        )
        # Position formula relative to title
        formula.next_to(title, DOWN, buff=0.7)
        
        # 3. Labeling the variables
        labels = VGroup(
            Text("n = Total Trials", font_size=20),
            Text("k = Successful Outcomes", font_size=20),
            Text("p = Probability of Success", font_size=20)
        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).next_to(formula, DOWN, buff=0.5)

        self.add(formula, labels)

        # 4. Visualization: Bar Chart for n=10, p=0.5
        n_val = 10
        p_val = 0.5
        probs = [comb(n_val, k) * (p_val**k) * ((1 - p_val)**(n_val - k)) for k in range(n_val + 1)]
        
        # Fixing TypeError: Mobject.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'x_label_constructor'
        # In Manim CE, the label constructor is specified within the axis_config dictionaries.
        chart = BarChart(
            values=probs,
            bar_names=[str(i) for i in range(n_val + 1)],
            y_range=[0, 0.3, 0.1],
            x_axis_config={
                "font_size": 18,
                "label_constructor": Text
            },
            y_axis_config={
                "font_size": 18,
                "label_constructor": Text
            },
        )
        chart.scale(0.7).to_edge(DOWN, buff=0.5)
        
        self.play(Create(chart))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial Setup
        title = "Key Metrics: Mean and Variance"
        lines = [
            "We can predict the average outcome using the mean.",
            "Multiplying trials by success probability gives the expected value.",
            "Standard deviation measures the typical spread around that average."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Display formulas Mean = n*p using Text to avoid LaTeX dependency
        mean_formula = Text("Mean = n × p", color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(mean_formula, "B2", "B5", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Write(mean_formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Display SD formula using Text to avoid LaTeX dependency
        sd_formula = Text("SD = √(n × p × (1 - p))", color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(sd_formula, "C2", "C5", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # Setup Gauge (n=100, p=0.7 means expected value is 70)
        gauge = NumberLine(
            x_range=[0, 100, 10],
            length=5,
            include_numbers=True,
            label_constructor=Text,
            font_size=16,
            color=WHITE
        )
        self.place_in_area(gauge, "E1", "E6", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        gauge_label = Text("Predicted Score Meter (n=100, p=0.7)", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(gauge_label, "D3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        needle = Arrow(
            start=UP * 0.6,
            end=ORIGIN,
            color="#FFFF00",
            buff=0,
            stroke_width=6
        )
        
        # Position needle at 0 initially
        needle.move_to(gauge.number_to_point(0) + UP * 0.3)
        
        self.play(
            Write(sd_formula),
            Create(gauge),
            FadeIn(gauge_label),
            FadeIn(needle)
        )
        
        # Animate needle to 70 (Mean = 100 * 0.7)
        self.play(needle.animate.move_to(gauge.number_to_point(70) + UP * 0.3), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(

import os
from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

outline.topic: Mastering the Binomial Distribution: From Coin Flips to Data Science
outline.target_audience: High school students and introductory college statistics learners

sections.title: The Prerequisite: The Bernoulli Trial
sections.content: Introduce the concept of a 'Bernoulli Trial' as the building block. A single event with exactly two outcomes: Success (p) or Failure (q = 1-p). This establishes the 'Yes/No' nature of the data before we scale up.
sections.example: Meet 'Byte the Robot'. Byte tries to throw a ball into a hoop. He either makes it (Success) or misses (Failure). We visualize a simple 0/1 switch flipping.

sections.title: Defining the Binomial Distribution (The BINS Test)
sections.content: Explain the four conditions required for a distribution to be Binomial using the acronym BINS: Binary (Success/Fail), Independent (One trial doesn't affect the next), Number (Fixed number of trials 'n'), and Same probability 'p' for every trial.
sections.example: Byte the Robot is now programmed to take 10 shots. Each shot is independent. We use a checklist overlay on the screen to verify if Byte's 10-shot session meets the BINS criteria.

sections.title: Visualizing the Formula: Combinations and Probability
sections.content: Break down the formula P(X=k) = nCk * p^k * (1-p)^(n-k). Focus on the 'Why': nCk represents the number of paths/ways to get exactly 'k' successes. p^k is the probability of the successes, and (1-p)^(n-k) is the probability of the failures occurring.
sections.example: Visualizing a Galton Board (Pachinko machine). Show the ball hitting pegs. Each peg is a choice. We highlight one specific 'path' to 3 successes out of 5 trials to explain the combination 'nCk' visually.

sections.title: The Shape of Probability: Histograms
sections.content: Demonstrate how the distribution looks when plotted as a histogram. Discuss how the peak moves based on the value of 'p' (skewness) and how it becomes a 'Bell Curve' (Normal approximation) as the number of trials 'n' increases.
sections.example: An animated graph where 'n' starts at 5 and grows to 50. The bars of the histogram become thinner and smoother, eventually looking like a mountain peak centered at n*p.

sections.title: Key Metrics: Mean and Variance
sections.content: Introduce simple formulas for the 'Expected Value' (Mean = n*p) and 'Standard Deviation' (Spread). This helps predict the 'average' outcome of the experiment over time.
sections.example: If Byte has a 70% success rate (p=0.7) and shoots 100 times (n=100), we show a 'Predicted Score' meter pointing at 70, with a 'shimmer' area representing the standard deviation.

sections.title: Real-World Application: Quality Control
sections.content: Apply the knowledge to a practical scenario like manufacturing or biology. This reinforces why the Binomial distribution is essential for predicting risk and success rates.
sections.example: A 'Dragon Egg' hatchery. If each egg has a 5% chance of being a rare Gold Dragon, what is the probability that a clutch of 20 eggs contains exactly 2 Gold Dragons? We calculate this live on screen using the Binomial logic.
